title: Ballistic-to-Localized Dynamics as Signature of Quantum Phase Transition in Josephson Junction
authors: F. G. Capone, A. de Candia, G. Di Bello, V. Cataudella, R. Fazio, N. Nagaosa, C. A. Perroni, G. De Filippis
abstract: Using state-of-the-art numerical techniques, we investigate how quantum phase fluctuations and quasiparticle tunneling shape the behavior of a small-capacitance Josephson junction across Ohmic, sub-Ohmic, and super-Ohmic dissipation regimes. We show that increasing the Ohmic dissipation strength drives a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless quantum phase transition at thermodynamic equilibrium. Deviations from Ohmic behavior profoundly alter this scenario: the super-Ohmic regime exhibits no phase transition, whereas the sub-Ohmic regime displays a continuous second-order transition, consistent with the universality classes of the spin-boson model. Within the Ohmic regime, real-frequency linear-response calculations reveal that the phase particle does not undergo the commonly assumed diffusive-to-localized crossover. Instead, finite resistance progressively suppresses the singular zero-frequency response, producing a ballistic-to-localized change in the dynamics. At finite frequencies, coupling to the environment generates a long-lived excitation in the charge response, which evolves into a resonance as the subgap and shunt resistances are reduced.
summary: This paper analyzes the quantum phase transition in a Josephson junction by studying its response to different levels of environmental dissipation. It demonstrates that the transition is governed by the dissipation regime, showing a BKT transition in the Ohmic case. Crucially, it reveals a ballistic-to-localized dynamic crossover, challenging simple diffusive models of quantum tunneling.
main_problem: The study investigates how quantum phase fluctuations and quasiparticle tunneling dictate the behavior of a Josephson junction across various dissipation regimes, aiming to pinpoint the signature of a Quantum Phase Transition (QPT).
main_result: The system exhibits a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) QPT in the Ohmic regime, while the dynamics show a ballistic-to-localized crossover, contradicting standard diffusive predictions.
method: The research employs advanced numerical techniques, including Worldline Monte Carlo (WLMC), Density-Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG), and real-frequency linear-response calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is a small-capacitance Josephson junction, modeled using an effective imaginary-time action incorporating charging energy, Josephson coupling, and dissipation characterized by a memory kernel.
key_observables: Order parameter ($m_2$), Binder cumulant ($u$), phase particle mobility ($\mu$), and the Drude weight ($D_Q$).
important_parameters: Dissipation exponent ($s$) defining Ohmic ($s=1$), sub-Ohmic ($s<1$), and super-Ohmic ($s>1$) regimes; coupling strength ($\alpha$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the low-energy dynamics to the spin-boson model and comparing results against the Caldeira-Leggett (CL) model.
figures_summary: Figures confirm the QPT via Binder cumulant crossings ($\alpha_c \approx 3.2$) and show the collapse of the bandwidth ($\Delta E$) as the transition is approached.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system across different dissipation regimes, first establishing the QPT signature using equilibrium methods, then detailing the dynamical crossover in the Ohmic regime, and finally comparing the results against established theoretical models like the spin-boson and polaronic models.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed theoretical understanding of how environmental coupling (dissipation) fundamentally alters the nature of quantum phase transitions in superconducting circuits, linking equilibrium critical points to measurable transport dynamics.
